blurb: Ancient Spanish sighthound bred to course hare, in smooth or rough coats
description: The Galgo Español, or Spanish Greyhound, is a lean Spanish sighthound bred to course hare, lighter than a Greyhound, with a smooth or rough coat.
answer: The Galgo Español, or Spanish Greyhound, is a Spanish sighthound bred specifically for coursing hare and other game. It resembles the Greyhound but is lighter, with flatter muscling suited to endurance. It stands about 58 to 72 cm and comes in smooth and rough coats.

body: Its origins are debated: it may descend from Sloughis brought during the Muslim conquest, or from the Celtic vertragus described by Arrian in Roman Iberia, later crossed with the Sloughi. The name probably comes from the Latin Canis Gallicus, dog from Gaul. In medieval Castile it was a noble dog, protected by laws against its theft or killing, and it appears in the opening sentence of Don Quixote. Early 20th-century crosses with English Greyhounds for track racing were eventually judged not worthwhile. In 2026 the Spanish kennel club listed it among sixteen vulnerable Spanish breeds.

Galgos are higher in the rear than the front, with flatter muscling than a Greyhound, a lighter build, a longer tail and a very long, streamlined head. The chest is not as deep and should not reach the elbow. Unlike Greyhounds, they come in smooth and rough coats, the rough coat giving extra protection in the field. Colours include brindle, black, golden, cinnamon, yellow, red, white and white with patches.
The source text gives little detail on temperament. It is described mainly as a swift hunting dog with long-distance running ability.

Sources give little specific detail on care. Galgos are used for hunting, racing and lure coursing, and as sighthounds bred for endurance they are generally thought to need regular chances to run. Reports of mistreatment by some hunters in Spain have led rescue associations to rehome many Galgos in Spanish cities and elsewhere in Europe.
Like many sighthounds, the Galgo is described as a fairly healthy breed, although it is reported to be sensitive to anaesthesia. Breed clubs generally recommend regular veterinary check-ups.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Galgo and a Greyhound?
faq.a: The Galgo is lighter, higher in the rear and has flatter muscling, a longer tail and a less deep chest. It also comes in a rough coat as well as a smooth one.

faq.q: How big does a Galgo Español get?
faq.a: It stands about 58 to 72 cm at the withers.

faq.q: Is the Galgo Español recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It is FCI breed number 285 in Group 10, Sighthounds.
